chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Rabi' ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
and was asked about al-Samad, so he said: Al-Samad is He who has no interior (hollow).
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Al-Samad' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) interprets 'al-Samad' not merely as the Eternal Refuge, but specifically as the One without a hollow or interior cavity, highlighting His absolute physical and metaphysical completeness. This definition serves to refute anthropomorphic views by affirming that while Allah possesses a form, He lacks the internal voids characteristic of created bodies, thereby distinguishing His unique essence from contingent matter. This interpretation underscores the divine attribute of self-sufficiency and unity, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in contrast to the multiplicity found in created beings.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. My Father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah related to me that Muhammad ibn `Isa ibn `Ubayd, on the authority of Yunus ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Muslim that
When asked about the Needless [al-Samad], I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim (AS) reply: “The Needless is He who has no interior.”
